original_question: Let Ω be a round spherical disc of radius α < π/2 on the unit sphere S^2, and let Ω′ be a convex domain in S^2 with the same area as Ω. Show that there exists a bi-Lipschitz map from Ω′ to the Euclidean plane whose Lipschitz constants are 1 and α/sin(α), that is, a (1, α/sin(α))-bi-Lipschitz map.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s intended statement: it has the correct ambient space (the unit sphere S²), the correct model set (a round disc of radius α with α < π/2), the correct comparison object (a convex domain Ω′ in S² of the same area), and the correct target conclusion, namely existence of a map to the plane with sharp bi-Lipschitz constants 1 and α/sin(α).
missing_details: Make explicit that Ω is a round geodesic disc in the standard round unit sphere S².
Specify that Ω′ is geodesically convex in S²; on the sphere, this is the intended meaning of convex.
State that the area comparison is with respect to spherical area on S².
Unpack the bi-Lipschitz condition as explicit inequalities for all x,y in Ω′, using the spherical geodesic distance on S² and the Euclidean distance in ℝ².
State the map explicitly as f: Ω′ → ℝ²; no surjectivity onto the whole plane is required.
Include the range 0 < α < π/2 explicitly so the question is stand-alone.
refined_question: Let Ω ⊂ S² be a round geodesic disc of radius α, where 0 < α < π/2, on the unit sphere S² with its standard spherical metric, and let Ω′ ⊂ S² be a geodesically convex domain whose spherical area equals that of Ω. Show that there exists a map f: Ω′ → ℝ² such that for all x,y ∈ Ω′, one has d_{S²}(x,y) ≤ |f(x) - f(y)| ≤ (α/sin(α)) d_{S²}(x,y), where d_{S²} denotes the spherical geodesic distance and |·| the Euclidean distance. In other words, Ω′ admits a (1, α/sin(α))-bi-Lipschitz map to the Euclidean plane.
justification: This is the exact open problem singled out in Section 11 of the paper. The surrounding context there shows that the paper is not asking for a broader extremal-distortion problem, but specifically for the same sharp constant as the round disc: the next sentence says that polar coordinates on the round disc give such a map and that the constant is optimal, and the following sentence notes that the perimeter variant is known. The only real work needed to make your draft fully stand-alone is to spell out the metric and area conventions and make explicit that convex means geodesically convex on S².
